customer_name: Shenzhen Environmental Water Group (深圳市环境水务集团)
business_problem: Shenzhen Environmental Water Group needed to scale resident-facing water services despite limited 'water steward' staff, inconsistent service knowledge, and the lack of round-the-clock availability across a very large utility footprint.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud worked with Shenzhen Environmental Water Group to develop the 'Thousands of Households Water Steward' intelligent agent on top of the group's existing Deepwater Cloud Brain AI foundation. The immediate focus was customer service, but the agent also feeds management and operations workflows. On the service side, the assistant acts as a 24x7 digital water steward that simulates human explanations for supply and drainage questions, intercepts routine inquiries before they reach staff, and responds with standard answers built from integrated business knowledge. The platform also breaks through data silos so the assistant can retrieve water-consumption information and work-order status quickly, giving both residents and staff a faster service loop. At the management layer, the system aggregates service data, monitors indicators in real time, and produces a 'warning-dispatch-analysis-iteration' closed loop that supports better resource allocation and precision service strategies. The result is a large-utility AI service model that blends front-line resident support with back-office decision intelligence.
products_used: Thousands of Households Water Steward Intelligent Agent

solution_components.name: Deepwater Cloud Brain
solution_components.role: Provides the underlying AI foundation that Shenzhen Environmental Water Group uses to extend large-model capabilities into utility operations and customer service.

solution_components.name: Thousands of Households Water Steward Intelligent Agent
solution_components.role: Handles resident consultations, knowledge retrieval, status checks, and management feedback loops for the water utility.

data_flow: Resident questions and utility service data enter the Water Steward agent, business knowledge and account/work-order data are retrieved from connected systems, answers or service guidance are returned to users, and the resulting service metrics are aggregated into real-time warning, dispatch, analysis, and iteration workflows for managers.
business_outcome: The group expanded utility-service coverage, reduced pressure on human water stewards, improved knowledge consistency, and gained a data-driven management loop for smarter service allocation.
